Hi Marie —

Appreciate the note and the context — good, clear asks. Quick summary up-front: we can preserve some feature behavior during a compact-tier pilot but there are engineering and pricing tradeoffs. Looping in Kimberly for the precise pricing and trade credit options; Ben for the capacity/latency implications.

High-level tradeoffs (short):
- Async batch export: technically possible to keep as a limited add-on on Compact (rate-limited); will increase per-export latency for very large batches.
- KV cache retention: default compact retention is shorter (2 hours) — extending to 24 hours requires either preserving a small dedicated cache pool or moving to a nearline cache offering that adds a small per-GB/day fee.
- Latency & burst: Compact is optimized to keep steady-state latency low for short sequences; large concurrent bursts can see queuing. We can provision a burst window but that carries a committed-cost component.

Next steps: Kimberly — can you outline 2 pricing scenarios we can present to Marie: (A) compact + limited-feature add-ons with a one-quarter transition credit, and (B) short-term Dedicated reserve for the pilot month(s) with rollback clauses? Please include expected delta in effective $/1000 tokens and any SLA differences.

Marie: I will follow up with a slide-style summary you can share with your CFO.

—Rohan
Principal Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Hi all —

Thanks for looping me in. I pulled numbers off the pilot usage Marie attached and sketched two pragmatic options. Notes below are intentionally concise so you can paste into a CFO brief.

Option A — Compact + Add-ons (recommended if cost is the primary constraint)
- What stays: Text generation, streaming, and core chat features.
- Add-ons available: Async batch export (rate-limited: 5 concurrent exports), KV cache retention extended to 24h via nearline cache (charged at $0.40/GB/day).
- Pricing impact: Compact base $/1k tokens = $0.45 (current pilot throughput $/1k = $0.68). Add-ons estimated: $900/month for cache + $250/month export overlay based on current volume.
- Transition credit: We can provide a one-quarter credit equal to 20% of add-on fees (applied as invoice credit) if you commit to a 6-month Compact term after the pilot.
- SLA: Compact + add-ons — standard Compact SLOs; export operations best-effort with 24-48h completion window for heavy batches.

Option B — Short Dedicated Reserve (recommended if burst reliability is critical)
- What stays: Full current feature set with dedicated pool for KV cache (no retention cap) and export throughput.
- Pricing impact: Effective $/1k tokens = $0.62 after amortizing a 1-month reserved capacity commit. Cost higher than Compact, but burst and export SLAs are guaranteed.
- Commitment: 1 month min reserve with a 3-month rolling option; we can include a rollback clause to Compact with 14-day notice (no refund of reserve but we can apply pro-rated account credits towards future consumption).

Quick recommendation: If your CFO is driven by near-term cost reduction and you can tolerate export latency, Option A with the 20% add-on credit is the lowest-risk way to show savings while keeping key features. If Clearwell needs guaranteed export windows for production workloads, Option B avoids operational surprise at higher cost.

Attachment: I exported a one-page comparison and a sample invoice math in "proposal_v2.pdf" (attached).

Happy to jump on a 20-minute call to walk through the numbers tomorrow.

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Head of Pricing & Commercial Ops, Redwood Inference
